Fall 2025 - Grain &
Storage Policies
CEDAR COUNTY COOP
  Sampling:
You may wait for the sample to be tested prior to dumping.
◦ If the hauler is not satisfied with the grade, a second sample will be taken.
◦ However, the grade obtained on the last sample will be used for settlement purposes.

The seller has the option of requesting official grades by a federal grain
inspector on any contested samples. The seller shall stand the cost of such
grades and these grades will be final.

We will retain all samples when grades are contested for 10 days.

We reserve the right to refuse corn in excess of 25% moisture.
 Delivery:
Information:
The hauler needs to give accurate, complete information to the scale operator. The owner's
name, split percentage if multiple owners, and the disposition of the grain, also notify us when
the last load is delivered so the settlement can be made promptly.

Open storage:
Grain delivered in January - September must be priced within 30 days or by October 1st
whichever comes first.

Grain delivered after October 1st will have maximum of 5 calendar days in open
storage. If no instructions are received on the disposition of the grain by the last day of open
storage, the grain will be sold.
 Purchase Agreement:
Grain purchase contracts are written for the exact net (dry) bushels.
Any over delivery will be purchased at the time of settlement.
Any under delivery will settle at the difference between the contract price and
the market price at the time of settlement.
 Moisture Levels:
Corn:
Corn is purchased at 15% moisture.
Corn for storage must be no more than 14%.
Corn for Grain Bank must be no more than 15%.
Corn above these levels will be dried and have shrink taken to the required moisture.

Soybeans:
Soybeans will be purchased and stored at 13% moisture or below.
 Corn Drying Charges:
Drying charge is 4 cents per point of moisture removed with a 1.4% shrink factor
figured to the nearest 1/10%.
Drying charges are computed from wet bushels.
 Soybean Drying Charges:
Beans purchased or for storage in excess of 13% moisture will be shrunk at the
rate of 1% for each ½% of moisture or fraction thereof over 13%.
 Storage Rates:
Corn:
◦ 17 cents minimum for first 90 days, 0.134 cents per bushel per day thereafter
Soybeans:
◦ 20 cents minimum for first 90 days, 0.167 cents per bushel per day thereafter
Grain Bank Corn:
◦ 3 cents per bushel per month
◦ Grain sold out of grain bank will revert to regular storage charges.
Warehouse Receipt:
◦ Minimum storage billed when warehouse receipt is issued. Balance of storage
  deducted at the time of settlement. Co-op will provide a release to CCC so that
  storage on sealed grain need not be prepaid.
 Price Later Program:
Price Later may possibly be used to gain ownership of grain to allow the Coop to
ship bushels. Last year we actively asked some customers to utilize this program
and we structure this to mirror the open storage charges for the year.
Corn:
◦ 17 cents minimum for first 90 days, 0.134 cents per bushel per day thereafter

Soybeans:
◦ 20 cents minimum for first 90 days, 0.167 cents per bushel per day thereafter

Note: Major difference is that ownership of the grain changes from the farmer
to the Coop
 Basis Only Contract:
Basis only is a tool that is used to set basis on grain and have futures pricing
ability at a later date to set the futures. This tool also transfers ownership of the
grain from the farmer to the Coop.
◦ Advantage’s
  ◦ The producer’s basis is locked in and the producer can roll that basis to forward months to allow time
    to price the futures.
  ◦ If crop size is not as robust as USDA is calculating we could see a significant rally during and/or post
    harvest.
◦ Disadvantage’s
  ◦ Basis rolls take into account the spread between futures months and it cost 1c to roll each forward
    futures month.
  ◦ Basis is locked in at harvest time basis levels. Often times post harvest basis values improve.
  ◦ Two Cent service fee on writing a basis contract.
 Questions?
